speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they worsen with certain movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.
I see you have a one-year history of burning pain and paresthesias in your neck and arms with increasing hand weakness over the last three months, along with a history of diabetes and hypertension. Given the combination of sensory changes and progressive motor weakness, I am concerned about cervical spine instability or myelopathy; can you describe any difficulty with balance, gait, or fine motor tasks like buttoning your shirt?
